title: Coldcard Vulnerability and Wallet Entropy Best Practices
content: There is a severe vulnerability you may presume is **affecting all coldcards initialized after 2020** regardless of model. Some models have more severe problems than others (mk3) but even newer models have effectively 72 bits of entropy instead of the desired 256. Your coins could be stolen without you doing anything wrong at all. if you have any doubt, and even if you aren't using coldcard, you should follow these steps to protect yourself from similar attacks in the future. **Immediate Action** Immediately move any coins in any coldcard to a new wallet with manually generated, skew corrected entropy and a minimum 16 character BIP39 password. You may still temporarily use your coldcard for this, but use none of the coldcard's entropy. If you cannot make new manual entropy at this time, use moving to a stronger passphrases wallet as a temporary measure. Setting a new passphrase is as simple as selecting "passphrase" from your wallet menu and inputting a sufficiently long passphrase (16 characters minimum). **Long Term Safety** Your long term goal is to move away from coldcard into a new, secure, airgapped wallet as soon as possible. We recommend seedsigner, krux, glacier protocol, and yeticold. DIY solutions you can verify. You must, regardless of what wallet you use, roll your own skew corrected entropy. Below are general instructions for dice and coins. You can generate unbiased entropy from coinflips by flipping the same coin twice, and applying the following mapping: - **Heads, Heads**: Discard. - **Tails, Tails**: Discard. - **Heads, Tails**: Add a 0 to your entropy. - **Tails, Heads**: Add a 1 to your entropy. You may also use dice, in which case you will roll a single dice in sets of 2 rolls. - **If roll 1 is larger than roll 2**, record a 1 bit. - **If roll 2 is larger than roll 1**, record a 0 bit. - **If the rolls are equal**, discard the result Do this until you have 256 ones and zeros. This is your entropy. **Seed Words** To create seed words from your entropy follow the BIP39 process as described at https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0039.mediawiki#generating-the-mnemonic . Start by SHA256 hashing your ones and zeros. Take the resulting output and steal the first 8 bits and appending it to the end of your initial 1's and 0's. Split your ones and zeros into sets of 11. These 11 digit binary strings are your seed words. You can convert them from binary into an integer and you will get a number. That number is the number the word is on the seed word list - which you can find at: https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0039/english.txt for English seeds. **Additional Support** Visit the Bitcoin discord at https://btcmaxis.com/discord if you require any assistance at all, or if you want to vent about how Coinkite should burn to the ground. We're here for you. **Attack Details** Any ColdCard running firmware with a version release including and newer than 2021-03-17T1724-v4.0.0 (Q has different version numbers, but all are affected) has a broken rng implementation which supplies insufficient entropy when generating mnemonics. This includes the Mk4, Q, and Mk5, who have 32 bits more entropy than affected Mk3 and Mk2s, but **this is not sufficient** to be cryptographically secure. This is caused by a mismanaging of the MICROPY_HW_ENABLE_RNG inside the libngu package introduced in v4 of the firmware. It is set as a integer value instead of undefined, and this falls back to a PRNG XOR'd with a PRNG seeded with the datetime. Our advice to anyone who had a ColdCard generate their mnemonic is to generate a new one as soon as is practicable safely. Even if you have an extension phrase, or dice rolls, unless you are _certain_ they included enough entropy to be secure on their own; the dice code and extension phrase code are OK, the ColdCard-provided entropy is the issue. If you have a multisig setup, consider any key in that multisig generated by a ColdCard to be compromised. A 3 of 3 with two keys generated by a ColdCard, for example, should be considered to be reduced to a 1 of 1 of the key not generated by a ColdCard. If you have at least 1 key not generated by a ColdCard, your coins aren't at risk, but you should still rotate your keys to restore the intended function of your multisig. For generating new mnemonics, the gold standard is Von-Neumann skew-corrected coinflips (ask us for info). An airgapped laptop is an invaluable tool. In multisig, you may be comfortable with some of the keys being generated by software, or a hardware device *other than a ColdCard*. If you don't feel comfortable with these options, generate a new mnemonic using dice rolls via your existing ColdCard. 99+ rolls for a 24-word mnemonic. Do not skimp. If you continue to use a ColdCard without a patch resolving this issue, be aware that the entropy is not high enough to cryptographically guarantee that you won't end up using the same nonce twice. Signing two messages with the same private key and nonce compromises the key. Do not reuse addresses (including receiving multiple times).
